# Exhibit Style Template - Design Specification

> Conclusion-first layout with Exhibit takeaway bars, ideal for data-driven strategic reports and executive presentations.

---

## I. Template Overview

| Property       | Description                                            |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Template Name** | exhibit (Exhibit Style Template)                    |
| **Use Cases**  | Strategic planning, executive reports, investment analysis, board presentations |
| **Design Tone** | Premium, refined, authoritative, data-driven, conclusion-first |
| **Theme Mode** | Dark theme (dark background + gradient accents + gold highlights) |

---

## II. Canvas Specification

| Property       | Value                         |
| -------------- | ----------------------------- |
| **Format**     | Standard 16:9                 |
| **Dimensions** | 1280 × 720 px                |
| **viewBox**    | `0 0 1280 720`                |
| **Page Margins** | Left/Right 40px, Top 20px, Bottom 40px |
| **Safe Area**  | x: 40-1240, y: 40-680        |

---

## III. Color Scheme

### Primary Colors

| Role           | Value       | Notes                            |
| -------------- | ----------- | -------------------------------- |
| **Primary Dark** | `#0D1117` | Cover, chapter, ending page backgrounds |
| **Content White** | `#FFFFFF` | Content page main background     |
| **Gradient Start Blue** | `#1E40AF` | Top gradient bar start point |
| **Gradient End Purple** | `#7C3AED` | Top gradient bar end point   |
| **Gold Accent** | `#D4AF37`  | Dividers, highlight decorations  |
| **Purple-Blue Accent** | `#6366F1` | Chapter numbers, secondary accents |

### Text Colors

| Role           | Value       | Usage                  |
| -------------- | ----------- | ---------------------- |
| **White Text** | `#FFFFFF`   | Primary text on dark backgrounds |
| **Light Gray Text** | `#9CA3AF` | Descriptions, subtitles |
| **Tertiary Text** | `#6B7280` | Footer, timestamps     |
| **Body Black** | `#111827`   | Body text on light backgrounds |

### Neutral Colors

| Role           | Value       | Usage                  |
| -------------- | ----------- | ---------------------- |
| **Card Background** | `#1F2937` | Dark card background |
| **Divider**    | `#E5E7EB`   | Dividers on light backgrounds |
| **Border Gray** | `#374151`  | Borders on dark backgrounds |

---

## IV. Typography System

### Font Stack

**Font Stack**: `Arial, "Helvetica Neue", sans-serif`

### Font Size Hierarchy

| Level | Usage            | Size | Weight  | Letter Spacing |
| ----- | ---------------- | ---- | ------- | -------------- |
| H1    | Cover main title | 56px | Bold    | 2px            |
| H2    | Page main title  | 28px | Bold    | 1px            |
| H3    | Section title    | 48px | Bold    | 2px            |
| H4    | Card title       | 18px | Bold    | 1px            |
| P     | Body content     | 14px | Regular | -              |
| High  | Highlighted data | 40px | Bold    | -              |
| Sub   | Auxiliary text   | 12px | Regular | -              |

---

## V. Page Structure

### General Layout

| Area           | Position/Height | Description                            |
| -------------- | --------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| **Top**        | y=0, h=6px      | Gradient decorative bar (blue-purple gradient) |
| **Header**     | y=20, h=60px    | Key message / page title               |
| **Content Area** | y=100, h=520px | Main content area                    |
| **Footer**     | y=660, h=60px   | Data source, confidential label, page number |

### Decorative Elements

- **Top Gradient Bar**: Blue-purple gradient (`#1E40AF` → `#7C3AED`), height 4-6px
- **Left Gold Line**: Gold (`#D4AF37`), width 4px, used for chapter page decoration
- **Grid Decoration**: Low-opacity line grid for a data/precision feel

---

## VI. Page Types

### 1. Cover Page (01_cover.svg)

- Dark background (`#0D1117`)
- Top gradient decorative bar
- Left gold vertical line decoration
- Main title + subtitle + project ID
- Right-side grid decoration
- Bottom date, confidential label, author info

### 2. Table of Contents Page (02_toc.svg)

- Dark background
- Top gradient bar
- Double vertical line separator `||` design (gold)
- Chapter numbers in purple-blue
- Right-side grid decoration
- Confidential label

### 3. Chapter Page (02_chapter.svg)

- Dark background
- Top gradient bar
- Left gold vertical line
- Large semi-transparent background number
- Chapter title + description
- Right-side grid decoration

### 4. Content Page (03_content.svg)

- White background
- Top gradient thin bar
- Dark key message bar (gold left decoration)
- Flexible content area
- Footer: data source, confidential label, page number

### 5. Ending Page (04_ending.svg)

- Dark background
- Top gradient bar
- Grid decoration background
- Centered thank-you message
- Gold divider
- Contact info card
- Confidential label + copyright

---

## VII. Layout Patterns

| Pattern            | Use Cases                      |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------ |
| **Single Column Centered** | Cover, ending            |
| **Left-Right Split (5:5)** | Data comparison         |
| **Left-Right Split (3:7)** | Chart + text            |
| **Matrix Grid**    | Multi-dimensional analysis     |
| **Waterfall Chart** | Financial analysis            |
| **Table**          | Data summary                   |

---

## VIII. Spacing Guidelines

| Element            | Value  |
| ------------------ | ------ |
| Card gap           | 20px   |
| Content block gap  | 24px   |
| Card padding       | 24px   |
| Card border radius | 8px    |
| Icon-to-text gap   | 10px   |

---

## IX. SVG Technical Constraints

### Mandatory Rules

1. viewBox: `0 0 1280 720`
2. Use `<rect>` elements for backgrounds
3. Use `<tspan>` for text wrapping (no `<foreignObject>`)
4. Use `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity` for transparency; no `rgba()`
5. Prohibited: `clipPath`, `mask`, `<style>`, `class`, `foreignObject`
6. Prohibited: `textPath`, `animate*`, `script`, `marker`/`marker-end`
7. Use `<polygon>` triangles for arrows instead of `<marker>`
8. Define gradients using `<defs>` with `<linearGradient>`

### PPT Compatibility Rules

- No `<g opacity="...">` (group opacity); set opacity on each child element individually
- Use overlay layers for image transparency
- Inline styles only; no external CSS or `@font-face`

---

## X. Placeholder Specification

Templates use `{{PLACEHOLDER}}` format placeholders. Common placeholders:

| Placeholder        | Description        |
| ------------------ | ------------------ |
| `{{TITLE}}`        | Main title         |
| `{{SUBTITLE}}`     | Subtitle           |
| `{{PROJECT_ID}}`   | Project ID         |
| `{{AUTHOR}}`       | Author             |
| `{{DATE}}`         | Date               |
| `{{PAGE_TITLE}}`   | Page title         |
| `{{KEY_MESSAGE}}`  | Key message (Exhibit) |
| `{{CHAPTER_NUM}}`  | Chapter number     |
| `{{CHAPTER_TITLE}}`| Chapter title      |
| `{{PAGE_NUM}}`     | Page number        |
| `{{SOURCE}}`       | Data source        |
| `{{CONTACT_NAME}}` | Contact person name |
| `{{CONTACT_INFO}}` | Contact information |
| `{{COPYRIGHT}}`    | Copyright info     |
| `{{LOGO}}`         | Logo text          |

---

## XI. Signature Design Elements

### Confidential Label

All pages display a centered `CONFIDENTIAL` label at the bottom in gold text.

### Exhibit Title Bar

Content pages feature a dark background + gold left decoration key message bar at the top, similar to the "Exhibit" style used by consulting firms.

### Grid Background

Chapter and ending pages use low-opacity grid line decoration to create a professional data analysis atmosphere.

---

## XII. Usage Instructions

1. Copy the template to the project directory
2. Select the appropriate page template based on content needs
3. Use placeholders to mark content that needs replacement
4. Ensure the confidential label displays correctly
5. Generate the final SVG through the Executor role

> Strategist should determine specific color values based on project content, industry, and brand colors

| Role | HEX | Purpose |
| ---- | --- | ------- |
| **Background** | `#......` | Page background (light theme typically white; dark theme dark gray/navy) |
| **Secondary bg** | `#......` | Card background, section background |
| **Primary** | `#......` | Title decorations, key sections, icons |
| **Accent** | `#......` | Data highlights, key information, links |
| **Secondary accent** | `#......` | Secondary emphasis, gradient transitions |
| **Body text** | `#......` | Main body text (dark theme uses light text) |
| **Secondary text** | `#......` | Captions, annotations |
| **Tertiary text** | `#......` | Supplementary info, footers |
| **Border/divider** | `#......` | Card borders, divider lines |
| **Success** | `#......` | Positive indicators (green family) |
| **Warning** | `#......` | Issue markers (red family) |

> **Reference**: Industry colors in `references/strategist.md` or `scripts/config.py` under `INDUSTRY_COLORS`

### Gradient Scheme (if needed, using SVG syntax)

```xml
<!-- Title gradient -->
<linearGradient id="titleGradient" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="100%">
  <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#[primary]"/>
  <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#[secondary accent]"/>
</linearGradient>

<!-- Background decorative gradient (note: rgba forbidden, use stop-opacity) -->
<radialGradient id="bgDecor" cx="80%" cy="20%" r="50%">

  <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#[primary]" stop-opacity="0"/>
</radialGradient>
```

| **Code** | - | Consolas | Monaco |
| **Emphasis** | [font name] | [font name] | [font name] |

> **Unit convention**: Use px uniformly (SVG native unit) to avoid pt/px conversion errors
> **Selection principle**: Font size is based on **content density**, not design style

# LLM Usage Landscape - Design Specification

## I. Project Information

| Item | Value |
| ---- | ----- |
| **Project Name** | The 2025 LLM Usage Landscape: Real-World Data from OpenRouter |
| **Canvas Format** | PPT 16:9 (1280×720) |
| **Page Count** | 7 slides |
| **Design Style** | C) Top Consulting — Exhibit Style |
| **Target Audience** | LLM industry professionals (R&D, product, investment) |
| **Use Case** | Data-driven industry analysis report, executive/investor briefing |
| **Created Date** | 2026-04-20 |
| **Template** | exhibit |

---

## II. Canvas Specification

| Property | Value |
| -------- | ----- |
| **Format** | PPT 16:9 |
| **Dimensions** | 1280×720 px |
| **viewBox** | `0 0 1280 720` |
| **Margins** | Left/Right 40px, Top 20px, Bottom 40px |
| **Content Area** | x: 40–1240, y: 40–680; safe content area y: 100–660 |

---

## III. Visual Theme

### Theme Style

- **Style**: Top Consulting / Exhibit
- **Theme**: Hybrid — dark cover/chapter/ending pages + white content pages
- **Tone**: Premium, refined, authoritative, data-driven, conclusion-first

### Color Scheme

| Role | HEX | Purpose |
| ---- | --- | ------- |
| **Background (dark)** | `#0D1117` | Cover, chapter, ending backgrounds |
| **Background (light)** | `#FFFFFF` | Content page backgrounds |
| **Card Background** | `#1F2937` | Dark cards, panels |
| **Gradient Start** | `#1E40AF` | Top gradient bar start |
| **Gradient End** | `#7C3AED` | Top gradient bar end |
| **Gold Accent** | `#D4AF37` | Dividers, highlight decorations, key message bar |
| **Purple-Blue Accent** | `#6366F1` | Chapter numbers, secondary accents |
| **White Text** | `#FFFFFF` | Primary text on dark backgrounds |
| **Light Gray Text** | `#9CA3AF` | Descriptions, subtitles on dark bg |
| **Body Black** | `#111827` | Body text on light backgrounds |
| **Secondary Text** | `#4B5563` | Captions, annotations on light bg |
| **Tertiary Text** | `#6B7280` | Footer, timestamps |
| **Divider** | `#E5E7EB` | Dividers on light backgrounds |
| **Border Gray** | `#374151` | Borders on dark backgrounds |
| **Success Green** | `#16A34A` | Positive WoW growth indicators |
| **Warning Red** | `#DC2626` | Negative WoW change indicators |
| **Highlight Blue** | `#3B82F6` | Table header bars, chart accents |

### Gradient Scheme

```xml
<!-- Top accent bar gradient -->
<linearGradient id="topBarGrad" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">
  <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#1E40AF"/>
  <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#7C3AED"/>
</linearGradient>
<!-- Key message bar gradient -->
<linearGradient id="keyMsgGrad" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">
  <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#1F2937"/>
  <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#111827"/>
</linearGradient>
```

---

## IV. Typography System

### Font Plan

**Recommended preset**: P5 (English-primary)

| Role | English | Fallback |
| ---- | ------- | -------- |
| **Title** | Arial | Helvetica Neue, sans-serif |
| **Body** | Arial | Calibri, sans-serif |
| **Code** | Consolas | Monaco |
| **Emphasis** | Arial Black | Impact |

**Font stack**: `Arial, "Helvetica Neue", Calibri, sans-serif`

### Font Size Hierarchy

**Baseline**: Body font size = 14px (dense data slides)

| Purpose | Size | Weight |
| ------- | ---- | ------ |
| Cover title | 52px | Bold |
| Cover subtitle | 22px | Regular |
| Chapter title | 44px | Bold |
| Page title (H2) | 26px | Bold |
| Key message bar | 16px | Bold |
| Section header | 18px | Bold |
| **Body content** | **14px** | Regular |
| Table cell | 13px | Regular |
| Chart label | 12px | Regular |
| Annotation / footer | 11px | Regular |

---

## V. Layout Principles

### Page Structure

- **Top gradient bar**: y=0, h=5px — blue-purple gradient, all pages
- **Header area**: y=20, h=55px — page title or key message bar
- **Content area**: y=85, h=580px — main content
- **Footer area**: y=675, h=45px — data source, page number, CONFIDENTIAL label

### Common Layout Modes

| Mode | Used In |
| ---- | ------- |
| **Centered dark hero** | Cover (slide 1) |
| **Table layout** | Slide 2 (Top 10 Models) |
| **Pie/Donut chart + text** | Slide 3 (Market Share) |
| **Three-column cards** | Slide 4 (Trends), Slide 7 (Takeaways) |
| **KPI cards + bar chart** | Slide 5 (Rising Stars) |
| **Two-column** | Slide 6 (App Ecosystem) |

### Spacing Specification

| Element | Value |
| ------- | ----- |
| Card gap | 20px |
| Content block gap | 24px |
| Card padding | 20px |
| Card border radius | 8px |
| Icon-text gap | 10px |

---

## VI. Icon Usage Specification

### Source

- **Built-in icon library**: 640+ icons
- **Usage method**: Placeholder format `{{icon:category/icon-name}}`

### Recommended Icon List

| Purpose | Icon | Page |
| ------- | ---- | ---- |
| Growth / trending up | `arrow-trend-up` | Slide 2, 5 |
| Decline / trending down | `arrow-trend-down` | Slide 2 |
| Chart / data | `chart-bar` | Slide 3 |
| Ranking / podium | `trophy` | Slide 2 |
| Insight / key point | `lightbulb` | Slide 7 |
| AI / robot | `robot` | Slide 4, 6 |
| Code / developer | `code` | Slide 6 |
| Globe / international | `globe` | Slide 4 |
| Rocket / fast growth | `rocket` | Slide 5 |
| Target | `target` | Slide 7 |

---

## VII. Chart Reference List

| Chart Type | Reference Template | Used In | Purpose |
| ---------- | ------------------ | ------- | ------- |
| `horizontal_bar_chart` | `templates/charts/horizontal_bar_chart.svg` | Slide 2 | Top 10 models ranking by token usage — presented as a table with inline bars |
| `donut_chart` | `templates/charts/donut_chart.svg` | Slide 3 | Provider market share by token volume |
| `kpi_cards` | `templates/charts/kpi_cards.svg` | Slide 5 | WoW growth metrics for rising-star models |
| `horizontal_bar_chart` | `templates/charts/horizontal_bar_chart.svg` | Slide 6 | Top apps by daily token volume |

---

## VIII. Image Resource List

No images required — pure data visualization design.

---

## IX. Content Outline

### Slide 01 — Cover

- **Layout**: Full dark hero, centered, single column
- **Title**: The 2025 LLM Usage Landscape: Real-World Data from OpenRouter
- **Subtitle**: Based on real-world API usage from millions of OpenRouter users · Latest week of March 2025
- **Headline metric**: 26T+ tokens processed this week
- **Footer**: Data source: OpenRouter Rankings · March 2025 · CONFIDENTIAL
- **Design**: Dark background `#0D1117`, top gradient bar, gold vertical line left, large headline number as decorative element

### Slide 02 — This Week's Top 10 Models

- **Layout**: Full-width data table with inline sparkline-style bars
- **Key message bar**: "Xiaomi's MiMo-V2-Pro leads with 3.96T tokens — Chinese providers hold 6 of 10 spots"
- **Chart**: Custom data table (rank, model, provider, weekly tokens, WoW change with colored arrows)
- **Data**:
  | Rank | Model | Provider | Weekly Tokens | WoW |
  |:---:|---|---|:---:|:---:|
  | 1 | MiMo-V2-Pro | Xiaomi | 3.96T | +165% |
  | 2 | Step 3.5 Flash (free) | Stepfun | 1.49T | +1% |
  | 3 | MiniMax M2.7 | MiniMax | 1.29T | +253% |
  | 4 | DeepSeek V3.2 | DeepSeek | 1.24T | +9% |
  | 5 | Claude Sonnet 4.6 | Anthropic | 1.04T | -0% |
  | 6 | Claude Opus 4.6 | Anthropic | 995B | +2% |
  | 7 | Gemini 3 Flash Preview | Google | 972B | +3% |
  | 8 | GLM 5 Turbo | Zhipu (z-ai) | 968B | -6% |
  | 9 | MiniMax M2.5 | MiniMax | 909B | -30% |
  | 10 | Grok 4.1 Fast | x-ai | 599B | +32% |
- **Highlight**: Chinese providers (Xiaomi, Stepfun, MiniMax ×2, DeepSeek, Zhipu) = 6 of top 10
- **Footer**: Source: OpenRouter Rankings · March 2025

### Slide 03 — Provider Market Share Breakdown

- **Layout**: Left donut chart (60%) + right ranked list with bar indicators (40%)
- **Key message bar**: "Xiaomi dominates at 25.9%; Chinese providers combined hold 54.3% of global token volume"
- **Chart**: Donut chart showing provider share; right panel shows ranked list
- **Data**:
  | Provider | Share | Tokens |
  |---|:---:|:---:|
  | Xiaomi | 25.9% | 1.31T |
  | Google | 11.8% | 594B |
  | Anthropic | 11.0% | 555B |
  | MiniMax | 8.5% | 429B |
  | OpenAI | 7.9% | 400B |
  | Stepfun | 6.8% | 341B |
  | DeepSeek | 6.6% | 334B |
  | Zhipu (z-ai) | 6.5% | 326B |
  | x-ai | 3.9% | 195B |
  | Others | 11.2% | 563B |
- **Callout**: Chinese providers combined (Xiaomi + MiniMax + Stepfun + DeepSeek + Zhipu) = 54.3%
- **Footer**: Source: OpenRouter Rankings · March 2025; Note: Provider share covers all models/apps, not only top-10

### Slide 04 — Shifts in the Market Landscape

- **Layout**: Three-column cards + headline stat at top
- **Key message bar**: "Token volume grew 13× in one year — from ~2T to ~26T weekly; Chinese models now define the market"
- **Content** (3 cards):
  1. **Chinese Models Dominate Globally** — On OpenRouter (an international platform), Chinese providers hold 54.3% combined share. Xiaomi, DeepSeek, MiniMax, Stepfun, and Zhipu now surpass the combined share of Google, Anthropic, and OpenAI.
  2. **Flash/Turbo Variants Far Outpace Flagships** — Step 3.5 Flash, GLM 5 Turbo, Gemini 3 Flash — "fast and affordable" models see far higher usage than flagship counterparts. Speed and cost beat peak benchmarks in real deployments.
  3. **Anthropic's Growth Has Stalled** — Despite holding two models in the top 10 (Claude Sonnet 4.6 at 1.04T and Claude Opus 4.6 at 995B), both show near-zero week-over-week growth (+2% / -0%), while competitors are posting triple-digit gains.
- **Headline stat**: 26T tokens/week vs ~2T one year ago = 13× market expansion
- **Footer**: Source: OpenRouter Rankings · March 2025

### Slide 05 — This Week's Rising Stars: Fastest-Growing Models

- **Layout**: KPI cards (top row, 3 cards) + supporting table (bottom)
- **Key message bar**: "MiniMax M2.7 surges +253% WoW — agentic and coding-specialized models lead the growth wave"
- **KPI cards** (top 3 fastest-growing):
  - MiniMax M2.7 · MiniMax · **+253%** WoW
  - MiMo-V2-Pro · Xiaomi · **+165%** WoW
  - Cline (coding agent) · Independent · **+128%** WoW
- **Supporting table** (additional fast-movers):
  | Model | Provider | WoW Growth | Driver |
  |---|---|:---:|---|
  | Ampere | Ampere | +576% | New entrant surge |
  | Codex | OpenAI | +112% | Coding agent demand |
  | Hermes Agent | Nous Research | +92% | Agentic workflow adoption |
- **Analysis**: Growth drivers — (1) Chinese model cost-performance; (2) agentic/coding specialization; (3) new entrant momentum
- **Footer**: Source: OpenRouter Rankings · March 2025

### Slide 06 — App Ecosystem: Who's Calling These Models

- **Layout**: Left horizontal bar chart (top apps) + right analysis cards
- **Key message bar**: "4 of the top 5 apps are AI coding tools — developer tooling is the #1 LLM consumption use case"
- **Chart**: Horizontal bar chart (daily token volume, top 10 apps)
- **Data**:
  | App | Daily Tokens | Category |
  |---|:---:|---|
  | OpenClaw | 829B | AI productivity / coding |
  | Kilo Code | 271B | VS Code AI coding |
  | Claude Code | 78B | CLI coding tool |
  | Cline | 69.1B | VS Code coding agent |
  | Janitor AI | 29.2B | Roleplay / entertainment |
  | ISEKAI ZERO | 28.8B | AI adventure game |
  | Descript | 27B | AI video/podcast editor |
  | Hermes Agent | 19.2B | AI agent |
  | Roo Code | 11.8B | VS Code coding |
  | Scripty | 9.95B | New tool |
- **Right panel analysis** (2 insight cards):
  - **Coding dominates**: Top 4 apps are all coding tools. OpenClaw alone consumes 829B tokens/day — nearly 3× the second-place app.
  - **Entertainment persists**: Roleplay/entertainment apps (Janitor AI, ISEKAI ZERO) maintain strong presence, signaling broad consumer LLM adoption beyond productivity.
- **Footer**: Source: OpenRouter Rankings · March 2025

### Slide 07 — Key Insights and Industry Implications

- **Layout**: Four-quadrant/four-card grid (2×2), dark ending style
- **Key message bar** (top): "Four forces reshaping the LLM industry — implications for R&D, product, and investment"
- **Four cards**:
  1. **Chinese Models Have Won the Global Usage Race** — On the largest neutral LLM API platform, Chinese providers hold 54.3% combined share. This is no longer a forecast — it is current market reality.
  2. **AI Coding Agents = The Primary Commercial Use Case** — 5 of the top 10 apps are coding tools. Developer tooling is where LLM ROI is being realized today; investment should follow usage.
  3. **No Winner-Takes-All — The Market Is Fragmented** — Top 10 models span 8 different providers. Competition is fierce; switching costs are low; no single model or provider has locked in the market.
  4. **Fast & Affordable Beats Flagship** — Flash/Turbo variants (Step 3.5 Flash, GLM 5 Turbo, Gemini 3 Flash) dominate usage over flagship models. Benchmark superiority does not translate to adoption if cost and latency are uncompetitive.
- **Design**: Dark background, gold accent cards, each card with a numbered badge
- **Footer**: Source: OpenRouter Rankings · March 2025 · CONFIDENTIAL

---

## X. Speaker Notes Requirements

- **File naming**: Match SVG names (e.g., `01_cover.md`, `02_top_models.md`)
- **Total notes file**: `notes/total.md`
- **Notes style**: Professional, conclusion-first, suitable for executive/investor audience
- **Presentation duration**: ~15 minutes total (~2 min/slide)
- **Purpose**: Inform + persuade (investment/product decision makers)

---

## XI. Technical Constraints Reminder

### SVG Generation Must Follow:

1. viewBox: `0 0 1280 720`
2. Background uses `<rect>` elements
3. Text wrapping uses `<tspan>` (`<foreignObject>` FORBIDDEN)
4. Transparency uses `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity`; `rgba()` FORBIDDEN
5. FORBIDDEN: `clipPath`, `mask`, `<style>`, `class`, `foreignObject`
6. FORBIDDEN: `textPath`, `animate*`, `script`, `marker`/`marker-end`
7. Arrows use `<polygon>` triangles instead of `<marker>`
8. Gradients defined in `<defs>` with `<linearGradient>`

### PPT Compatibility Rules:

- `<g opacity="...">` FORBIDDEN (group opacity); set on each child element individually
- Inline styles only; external CSS and `@font-face` FORBIDDEN

---

## XII. Design Checklist

### Pre-generation

- [x] Content fits page capacity
- [x] Layout mode selected correctly
- [x] Colors used semantically (green = growth, red = decline, gold = key)
- [x] All data sourced from source_brief.md — no fabrication

### Post-generation

- [ ] viewBox = `0 0 1280 720`
- [ ] No `<foreignObject>` elements
- [ ] All text readable (>=11px)
- [ ] Content within safe area
- [ ] CONFIDENTIAL label on all pages

---

## XIII. Next Steps

1. ✅ Design spec complete — No AI images needed
2. **Next step**: Invoke **Executor** role (Top Consulting style) to generate SVGs

11	---
12	
13	## SCQA Framework (Narrative Structure)
14	
15	Every MBB-level presentation follows the SCQA narrative structure:
16	
17	| Element | Purpose | Typical Pages |
18	|---------|---------|---------------|
19	| **S - Situation** | Establish shared context | Cover / Pages 1-2 |
20	| **C - Complication** | Introduce the problem / tension | Pages 2-3 |
21	| **Q - Question** | The implicit or explicit question to solve | Transition page |
22	| **A - Answer** | Core solution | All body pages |
23	
24	**Page sequencing**: Cover embodies S+C → Executive Summary answers Q → Chapters develop A → Closing revisits S
25	
26	**Title writing**:
27	
28	| SCQA Element | Weak Title | MBB-level Title |
29	|-------------|------------|-----------------|
30	| S | "Industry Background" | "Digital penetration surpasses 60%, industry enters deep waters" |
31	| C | "Challenges Faced" | "Yet three structural contradictions constrain scaled deployment" |
32	| Q | "Strategic Question" | "How to move from pilot to full deployment within 18 months?" |
33	| A | "Solution" | "Three-phase path: Focus, Expand, Scale" |
34	
35	---
36	
37	## Data Contextualization (Never Present Data in Isolation)
38	
39	> **Golden Rule**: Never display a single data point in isolation. Every number needs context.
40	
41	| Method | Pattern | Visual Implementation |
42	|--------|---------|----------------------|
43	| **Time comparison** | "From X to Y" | Line chart + arrow annotating magnitude of change |
44	| **Benchmark** | "X vs industry average Y" | Bar chart with gray dashed baseline |
45	| **Competitive comparison** | "Us X vs Competitor Y" | Side-by-side bar chart, highlight own data |
46	| **Target gap** | "Actual X / Target Y" | Progress bar + gap annotation |
47	| **Ranking** | "Ranked #N of M" | Horizontal bar chart + highlight marker |
48	
49	**Data annotation three essentials**: Every data visualization must include (1) The value itself (large bold font) (2) Comparison reference (baseline / prior period / competitor) (3) Meaning interpretation ("So what?")
50	
51	```xml
52	<text x="160" y="280" text-anchor="middle" font-size="42" font-weight="bold" fill="#1E293B">97.3%</text>
53	<text x="160" y="310" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#64748B">Industry avg 82% | Competitor A 89%</text>
54	<text x="160" y="335" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="#059669">Leading industry by 15.3 percentage points</text>
55	```
56	
57	---
58	
59	## Pyramid Principle (Conclusion First)
60	
61	> Executives don't care about your *process* — they care about *results*.
62	
63	```
64	         ┌─────────────────┐
65	         │  Core Conclusion │   ← Page title / Takeaway
66	         └────────┬────────┘
67	      ┌───────────┼───────────┐
68	  ┌───┴───┐  ┌───┴───┐  ┌───┴───┐
69	  │ Arg 1 │  │ Arg 2 │  │ Arg 3 │   ← Key supporting points
70	  └───────┘  └───────┘  └───────┘
71	```
72	
73	| Level | Position | Font Size |
74	|-------|----------|-----------|
75	| Core conclusion | Takeaway Box | 16-18px bold |
76	| Arguments | Content area body | 14-16px |
77	| Supporting data | Charts / cards | 12-14px |
78	
79	**Contrast**: Title "Market Research Results" (wrong) → "Metaverse needs 5-10 years to reach scale" (right); Body "We researched... and found..." (wrong) → "Three arguments: (1)... (2)... (3)..." (right)
80	
81	---
82	
83	## MBB-level Layout Patterns
84	
85	### Content Page Standard Structure (1280x720)
86	
87	```
88	┌──────────────────────────────────┐
89	│ Gradient top bar (0,0 → 1280,6)  │
90	├──────────────────────────────────┤
91	│ Assertion title (x=40, y=50, 24px)│
92	├──────────────────────────────────┤
93	│ Takeaway Box (x=40, y=75,        │  ← Dark background + white text, one-sentence conclusion
94	│   w=1200, h=45)                  │
95	├──────────────────────────────────┤
96	│ Content area (x=40, y=140,       │  ← Charts / data / analysis
97	│   w=1200, h=520)                 │
98	├──────────────────────────────────┤
99	│ Source | CONFIDENTIAL | Page #    │  ← y=700, 10px
100	└──────────────────────────────────┘
101	```
102	
103	### Strategic Roadmap
104	
105	Three phases laid out horizontally, `<rect rx="8">` + title + action list, `<polygon>` arrows connecting:
106	
107	```
108	Focus Core (0-6mo)  ──>  Expand Capability (6-12mo)  ──>  Scale Up (12-18mo)
109	x=40,w=380              x=450,w=380                     x=860,w=380
110	```
111	
112	### Benchmarking Matrix
113	
114	Horizontal table; own row highlighted in theme color, others in gray. Leading indicators marked green, lagging marked red. Use `<circle>` or `<rect>` to build score points.
115	
116	### Waterfall Chart (Change Attribution)
117	
118	Start → increase/decrease factors → End. Positive factors green bars, negative factors red bars, start/end points dark bars, cumulative line as dashed connector.
119

122	## Strategic Use of Color
123	
124	MBB-level color usage is extremely restrained — color serves information:
125

138

141	| Comparing 2-7 categories | **Bar chart** | Visual comparison is intuitive |

37	Must output confirmation including: canvas dimensions, body font size, color scheme (primary/secondary/accent HEX values), font plan.
38	
39	**Why is this step mandatory?** Prevents the "spec says one thing, execution does another" disconnect.
40	
41	---
42	
43	## 3. Execution Guidelines
44	
45	- **Proximity principle**: Place related elements close together to form visual groups; increase spacing between unrelated groups to reinforce logical structure
46	- **Absolute spec adherence**: Strictly follow the color, layout, canvas format, and typography parameters in the spec
47	- **Follow template structure**: If templates exist, inherit the template's visual framework
48	- **Phased batch generation** (recommended):

50	  2. **Logic Construction Phase**: After all SVGs are finalized, batch-generate speaker notes to ensure narrative coherence (Narrative Continuity)
51	- **Technical specifications**: See [shared-standards.md](shared-standards.md) for SVG technical constraints and PPT compatibility rules
52	
53	### SVG File Naming Convention
54	
55	File naming format: `<number>_<page_name>.svg`
56	
57	- **Chinese content** → Chinese naming: `01_封面.svg`, `02_目录.svg`, `03_核心优势.svg`
58	- **English content** → English naming: `01_cover.svg`, `02_agenda.svg`, `03_key_benefits.svg`
59	- **Number rules**: Two-digit numbers, starting from 01
60	- **Page name**: Concise and descriptive, matching the page title in the Design Specification & Content Outline
61	
62	---
63	
64	## 4. Icon Usage
65	
66	Four approaches: **A: Emoji** (`<text>🚀</text>`) | **B: AI-generated** (SVG basic shapes) | **C: Built-in library** (`templates/icons/` 640+ icons, recommended) | **D: Custom** (user-specified)
67

69	
70	```xml

72	```
73	
74	> No need to manually run `embed_icons.py`; `finalize_svg.py` post-processing tool will auto-embed icons.
75	
76	**Common icons**: `chart-bar` `arrow-trend-up` `users` `cog` `circle-checkmark` `target` `clock` `file` `dollar` `lightbulb`

78	> ⚠️ **Icon validation rule**: If the Design Specification includes an icon inventory list, Executor may **only** use icons from that approved list. Using icon names not in the index is FORBIDDEN — verify against `templates/icons/icons_index.json` if uncertain.
79	
80	Full index: `templates/icons/README.md`

84	## 5. Chart Reference
85	
86	When the Design Spec includes a **VII. Chart Reference List**, read the referenced SVG templates from `templates/charts/` to understand common chart patterns.

88	**Adaptation rules**:

92	- **Must NOT**: Change chart type without Design Spec justification, or remove data points specified in the outline
93	
94	> Chart templates: `templates/charts/` (33 types). Index: `templates/charts/charts_index.json`

98	## 6. Image Handling
99	
100	Handle images based on their status in the Design Specification's "Image Resource List":
101	
102	| Status | Source | Handling |
103	|--------|--------|----------|
104	| **Existing** | User-provided | Reference images directly from `../images/` directory |
105	| **AI-generated** | Generated by Image_Generator | Images already in `../images/`, reference directly |
106	| **Placeholder** | Not yet prepared | Use dashed border placeholder |
107	
108	**Reference**: `<image href="../images/xxx.png" ... preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>`

110	**Placeholder**: Dashed border `<rect stroke-dasharray="8,4" .../>` + description text

118	| Role | Chinese Recommended | English Recommended |

121	| Body font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Calibri / Times |
122	| Emphasis font | SimHei | Arial Black / Consolas |
123	| Annotation font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Arial / Times |

127	## 8. Speaker Notes Generation Framework

129	### Task 1. Generate Complete Speaker Notes Document
130	
131	After **all SVG pages are generated and finalized**, enter the "Logic Construction Phase" and generate the complete speaker notes document in `notes/total.md`.
132	
133	**Why not generate page-by-page?** Batch-writing notes allows planning transitions like a script, ensuring coherent presentation logic.

151

153	
154	Automatically split `notes/total.md` into individual speaker note files in the `notes/` directory.

# Executor Common Guidelines

> Style-specific content is in the corresponding `executor-{style}.md`. Technical constraints are in shared-standards.md.

---

## 1. Template Adherence Rules

If template files exist in the project's `templates/` directory, the template structure must be followed:

| Page Type | Corresponding Template | Adherence Rules |
|-----------|----------------------|-----------------|
| Cover | `01_cover.svg` | Inherit background, decorative elements, layout structure; replace placeholder content |
| Chapter | `02_chapter.svg` | Inherit numbering style, title position, decorative elements |
| Content | `03_content.svg` | Inherit header/footer styles; **content area may be freely laid out** |
| Ending | `04_ending.svg` | Inherit background, thank-you message position, contact info layout |
| TOC | `02_toc.svg` | **Optional**: Inherit TOC title, list styles |

### Page-Template Mapping Declaration (Required Output)

Before generating each page, you must explicitly output which template (or "free design") is used:

```
📝 **Template mapping**: `templates/01_cover.svg` (or "None (free design)")
🎯 **Adherence rules / layout strategy**: [specific description]
```

- **Content pages**: Templates only define header and footer; the content area is freely laid out by the Executor
- **No template**: Generate entirely per the Design Specification & Content Outline

---

## 2. Design Parameter Confirmation (Mandatory Step)

> Before generating the first SVG page, you **must review the key design parameters from the Design Specification & Content Outline** to ensure all subsequent generation strictly follows the spec.

Must output confirmation including: canvas dimensions, body font size, color scheme (primary/secondary/accent HEX values), font plan.

**Why is this step mandatory?** Prevents the "spec says one thing, execution does another" disconnect.

---

## 3. Execution Guidelines

- **Proximity principle**: Place related elements close together to form visual groups; increase spacing between unrelated groups to reinforce logical structure
- **Absolute spec adherence**: Strictly follow the color, layout, canvas format, and typography parameters in the spec
- **Follow template structure**: If templates exist, inherit the template's visual framework
- **Phased batch generation** (recommended):
  1. **Visual Construction Phase**: Generate all SVG pages continuously, ensuring high consistency in design style and layout coordinates (Visual Consistency)
  2. **Logic Construction Phase**: After all SVGs are finalized, batch-generate speaker notes to ensure narrative coherence (Narrative Continuity)
- **Technical specifications**: See [shared-standards.md](shared-standards.md) for SVG technical constraints and PPT compatibility rules

### SVG File Naming Convention

File naming format: `<number>_<page_name>.svg`

- **Chinese content** → Chinese naming: `01_封面.svg`, `02_目录.svg`, `03_核心优势.svg`
- **English content** → English naming: `01_cover.svg`, `02_agenda.svg`, `03_key_benefits.svg`
- **Number rules**: Two-digit numbers, starting from 01
- **Page name**: Concise and descriptive, matching the page title in the Design Specification & Content Outline

---

## 4. Icon Usage

Four approaches: **A: Emoji** (`<text>🚀</text>`) | **B: AI-generated** (SVG basic shapes) | **C: Built-in library** (`templates/icons/` 640+ icons, recommended) | **D: Custom** (user-specified)

**Built-in icons — Placeholder method (recommended)**:

```xml
<use data-icon="chart-bar" x="100" y="200" width="48" height="48" fill="#005587"/>
```

> No need to manually run `embed_icons.py`; `finalize_svg.py` post-processing tool will auto-embed icons.

**Common icons**: `chart-bar` `arrow-trend-up` `users` `cog` `circle-checkmark` `target` `clock` `file` `dollar` `lightbulb`

> ⚠️ **Icon validation rule**: If the Design Specification includes an icon inventory list, Executor may **only** use icons from that approved list. Using icon names not in the index is FORBIDDEN — verify against `templates/icons/icons_index.json` if uncertain.

Full index: `templates/icons/README.md`

---

## 5. Chart Reference

When the Design Spec includes a **VII. Chart Reference List**, read the referenced SVG templates from `templates/charts/` to understand common chart patterns.

**Adaptation rules**:
- **Must preserve**: Chart type (bar/line/pie etc.) as specified in the Design Spec
- **Must adapt**: Data values, labels, colors (match the project's color scheme), and dimensions to fit the page layout
- **May adjust**: Axis ranges, grid lines, legend position, spacing — as long as the chart remains accurate and readable
- **Must NOT**: Change chart type without Design Spec justification, or remove data points specified in the outline

> Chart templates: `templates/charts/` (33 types). Index: `templates/charts/charts_index.json`

---

## 6. Image Handling

Handle images based on their status in the Design Specification's "Image Resource List":

| Status | Source | Handling |
|--------|--------|----------|
| **Existing** | User-provided | Reference images directly from `../images/` directory |
| **AI-generated** | Generated by Image_Generator | Images already in `../images/`, reference directly |
| **Placeholder** | Not yet prepared | Use dashed border placeholder |

**Reference**: `<image href="../images/xxx.png" ... preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>`

**Placeholder**: Dashed border `<rect stroke-dasharray="8,4" .../>` + description text

---

## 7. Font Usage

Apply corresponding fonts for different text roles based on the font plan in the Design Specification & Content Outline:

| Role | Chinese Recommended | English Recommended |
|------|--------------------|--------------------|
| Title font | Microsoft YaHei / KaiTi / SimHei | Arial / Georgia |
| Body font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Calibri / Times |
| Emphasis font | SimHei | Arial Black / Consolas |
| Annotation font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Arial / Times |

---

## 8. Speaker Notes Generation Framework

### Task 1. Generate Complete Speaker Notes Document

After **all SVG pages are generated and finalized**, enter the "Logic Construction Phase" and generate the complete speaker notes document in `notes/total.md`.

**Why not generate page-by-page?** Batch-writing notes allows planning transitions like a script, ensuring coherent presentation logic.

**Format**: Each page starts with `# <number>_<page_title>`, separated by `---` between pages. Each page includes: script text (2-5 sentences), `Key points: ① ② ③`, `Duration: X minutes`. Except for the first page, each page's text starts with a `[Transition]` phrase.

**Basic stage direction markers** (common to all styles):

| Marker | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `[Pause]` | Whitespace after key content, letting the audience absorb |
| `[Transition]` | Standalone paragraph at the start of each page's text, bridging from the previous page |

> Each style may extend with additional markers (`[Interactive]`/`[Data]`/`[Scan Room]`/`[Benchmark]` etc.), see `executor-{style}.md`.

**Requirements**:

- Notes should be conversational and flow naturally
- Highlight each page's core information and presentation key points
- Users can manually edit and override in the `notes/` directory

### Task 2. Split Into Per-Page Note Files

Automatically split `notes/total.md` into individual speaker note files in the `notes/` directory.

**File naming convention**:

- **Recommended**: Match SVG names (e.g., `01_cover.svg` → `notes/01_cover.md`)
- **Compatible**: Also supports `slide01.md` format (backward compatibility)

---

## 9. Next Steps After Completion

> **Auto-continuation**: After Visual Construction Phase (all SVG pages) and Logic Construction Phase (all notes) are complete, the Executor proceeds directly to the post-processing pipeline.

**Post-processing & Export** (see [shared-standards.md](shared-standards.md)):

```bash
# 1. Split speaker notes
python3 scripts/total_md_split.py <project_path>

# 2. SVG post-processing (auto-embed icons, images, etc.)
python3 scripts/finalize_svg.py <project_path>

# 3. Export PPTX
python3 scripts/svg_to_pptx.py <project_path> -s final
# Default: generates native shapes (.pptx) + SVG reference (_svg.pptx)
```

arguments.content:
# 01_cover

Welcome everyone. Today I'm presenting a snapshot of the LLM market that may surprise you — this is not a forecast based on model benchmarks, but real usage data from OpenRouter, one of the world's largest LLM API aggregation platforms. [Pause]

The headline number: over 26 trillion tokens were processed through OpenRouter in a single week in March 2025. One year ago, that figure was approximately 2 trillion. [Data] That is a 13× expansion in twelve months. [Pause]

What the data shows is a market in flux — new leaders, stalled incumbents, and a usage pattern that diverges sharply from what benchmark leaderboards would suggest.

Key points: (1) Data source: OpenRouter Rankings, March 2025 (2) Headline metric: 26T+ tokens/week (3) Market growing 13× year-over-year
Duration: 1 minute

---

# 02_top_models

[Transition] Let's start with the most direct signal: which models are people actually using?

The top 10 this week is led by Xiaomi's MiMo-V2-Pro at 3.96 trillion tokens — a number that is nearly 3× the second-place model. [Pause]

[Data] Six of the top 10 models are from Chinese providers: Xiaomi, Stepfun, MiniMax — appearing twice — DeepSeek, and Zhipu. This is on OpenRouter, an international platform predominantly used by developers and businesses outside China. [Benchmark] Anthropic holds two spots — #5 and #6 — combining for roughly 2 trillion tokens, but both show near-zero week-over-week growth while rivals post triple-digit gains.

[Scan Room] The growth column deserves particular attention: MiniMax M2.7 is up 253%. MiMo-V2-Pro is up 165%. These are not rounding errors — this is a structural shift.

Key points: (1) Xiaomi MiMo-V2-Pro leads at 3.96T tokens (2) Chinese providers hold 6/10 spots on international platform (3) Anthropic near-zero WoW growth vs competitors +100%+
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 03_market_share

[Transition] The individual model rankings tell one story. The provider-level market share tells an even clearer one.

[Data] Six of the top 10 models are from Chinese providers: Xiaomi, Stepfun, MiniMax — appearing twice — DeepSeek, and Zhipu. This is on OpenRouter, an international platform predominantly used by developers and businesses outside China. [Benchmark] Anthropic holds two spots — #5 and #6 — combining for roughly 2 trillion tokens, but both show near-zero week-over-week growth while rivals post triple-digit gains.

[Scan Room] The growth column deserves particular attention: MiniMax M2.7 is up 253%. MiMo-V2-Pro is up 165%. These are not rounding errors — this is a structural shift.

Key points: (1) Xiaomi MiMo-V2-Pro leads at 3.96T tokens (2) Chinese providers hold 6/10 spots on international platform (3) Anthropic near-zero WoW growth vs competitors +100%+
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 03_market_share

[Transition] The individual model rankings tell one story. The provider-level market share tells an even clearer one.

Xiaomi alone holds 25.9% of all token volume. [Benchmark] That is more than double Google at 11.8%, and more than double Anthropic at 11.0%. [Pause]

[Data] When we combine the five Chinese providers — Xiaomi, MiniMax, Stepfun, DeepSeek, and Zhipu — their combined share reaches 54.3%. More than half the global LLM API market, by token volume, on an international platform. [Pause]

One important note: OpenAI ranks fifth at 7.9%. In the public narrative, OpenAI is still frequently described as the market leader. The usage data tells a different story.

[Scan Room] I'd note that these figures represent total provider share across all models and apps on the platform — not just the top-10 model ranking — so they are directionally representative of broad market demand.

Key points: (1) Xiaomi #1 at 25.9% — more than double #2 and #3 (2) Chinese providers combined: 54.3% (3) OpenAI ranks #5 at 7.9% — narrative vs. reality gap
Duration: 2 minutes
Flex: [If time is tight, skip the OpenAI commentary and go directly to the next slide]

---

# 04_market_shifts

[Transition] Behind the rankings and the pie chart, three structural shifts define the current market dynamics.

First: Chinese models have not just entered the global market — they now define it. On a platform where users can choose any model in the world, they are choosing Chinese models more than half the time. [Pause] The cost-performance advantage is not theoretical — it is visible in every usage table.

Second: Flash and Turbo variants consistently outpace flagship models. Step 3.5 Flash ranks #2. Gemini 3 Flash is #7. GLM 5 Turbo is #8. Users are making a pragmatic choice: in production deployments, latency and cost matter more than the last few percentage points on a benchmark. [Benchmark] MMLU scores do not correlate with adoption when a cheaper, faster model exists.

Third: Anthropic holds two models in the top 10, but both show near-zero growth while the market is expanding at 13× year-over-year. [Pause] The market is growing rapidly around them without lifting their growth rate.

[Scan Room] This is the complication — a rapidly expanding market where the premium incumbents are not capturing growth.

Key points: (1) Chinese models dominant globally — cost-performance is proven, not projected (2) Flash/Turbo variants beat flagship in real usage — speed and cost trump benchmarks (3) Anthropic's growth has stalled despite top-10 presence
Duration: 3 minutes

---

# 05_rising_stars

[Transition] Within this expanding market, some models are accelerating dramatically — and the pattern reveals where the next wave of usage is forming.

MiniMax M2.7 grew 253% week-over-week. Xiaomi's MiMo-V2-Pro grew 165%. Cline, an autonomous VS Code coding agent, grew 128%. [Pause]

[Data] Even more striking: Ampere, a new entrant, posted 576% growth — the classic first-week surge of a model catching product-market fit early. OpenAI's Codex grew 112%, driven by coding agent demand. Hermes Agent from Nous Research grew 92%, reflecting broader agentic workflow adoption.

The pattern is clear: the fastest-growing models share two characteristics — they are either from cost-competitive Chinese providers, or they are purpose-built for coding and agentic workflows. [Pause] Generalist models are not the growth story. Specialized, fast, and affordable models are.

Key points: (1) MiniMax M2.7 +253%, MiMo-V2-Pro +165%, Cline +128% (2) Growth concentrated in Chinese models and coding/agentic specialists (3) New entrants can surge quickly — Ampere +576%
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 06_app_ecosystem

[Transition] Who is actually running these models? The app-level data reveals where the demand originates.

[Data] OpenClaw consumes 829 billion tokens per day — nearly 3× the second-place app. It is an AI productivity assistant built for autonomous task execution. Kilo Code, Claude Code, and Cline round out the top 4 — all AI coding tools. [Pause]

Four of the top five applications are coding tools. This is not a coincidence — it reflects the single largest commercial value proposition for LLMs today: helping developers write, review, and deploy code faster.

[Benchmark] For context: the entire entertainment and roleplay category — Janitor AI at 29B, ISEKAI ZERO at 28B — is roughly equivalent to one mid-tier coding app. The signal is clear.

[Scan Room] For anyone evaluating where to deploy LLM capabilities, the usage data gives a direct answer: start with developer tooling.

Key points: (1) Top 4 apps are all AI coding tools (2) OpenClaw 829B tokens/day — 3× the second place (3) Entertainment persists but coding dominates by an order of magnitude
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 07_key_insights

[Transition] Let me close with four implications distilled from everything we've seen.

First: Chinese models have won the global usage race — today, not eventually. 54.3% combined share on an international platform is not a trend to monitor; it is a market condition to respond to.

Second: AI coding agents are the primary commercial use case. This is where LLM ROI is being demonstrated at scale. Investment, R&D prioritization, and product roadmaps should follow actual usage concentration — not hypothetical future use cases. [Pause]

Third: The market is highly fragmented. No single model or provider has locked in the ecosystem. Switching costs are low. Multi-model strategies that route to the best model for each task will outperform single-provider bets.

Fourth: Fast and affordable beats flagship in real usage. Benchmark superiority that does not translate into latency and cost advantages will not drive adoption. Build for speed and economics first.

[Pause] The strategic implication across all four: the LLM market is moving faster than any single incumbent can keep pace with. The winners — for builders, for investors, and for product teams — are those who read the usage data and position accordingly.

[Scan Room] I'm happy to open up to questions on any of these four themes.

Key points: (1) Chinese dominance is current reality — requires strategic response (2) Code is the killer app — concentrate resources there (3) Fragmentation = multi-model strategies win (4) Speed + cost beats benchmarks in production
Duration: 3 minutes
Flex: [Cards 3 and 4 can be covered in 60 seconds each if time is short]
